assumptions: The zero-cost trade guard is the check whose triggering is described by the intent.
The matched base and quote amounts are observable quantities at guard evaluation time.

unresolved.description: The report does not quote the exact zero-cost check expression or its operands, so the guard's internal condition cannot be bound beyond the stated intent that it should trigger only when one side receives tokens without sending any.

The report does not specify whether matched base and quote amounts are caller-supplied inputs or derived from order state, so the disjoint-bits precondition is encoded as a grounded Boolean rather than a numeric bitwise relation.

limitations: The disjoint-bits precondition is represented as a single grounded Boolean because the report gives only illustrative examples (256 vs 1..255, 40 & 21) and no single numeric relation over named amount symbols.

The intent's 'only when' is encoded as a required-effect obligation on the guard trigger under the one-side-receives-without-sending condition; the report does not state the converse prohibition explicitly beyond the 'only when' wording.
